## Microbiome Training

Learning Goals:

Understand overview of workflow in taxonomic profiling studies.

Focus is on human gut microbiota.

## Needed Packages:

```{r}
#We need packages from cran and bioc, but only specific ones so we will set the ones that need install. 
cran_pkg <- c("BiocManager", "bookdown", "dplyr", "ecodist", "ggplot2", 
              "gridExtra", "kableExtra", "knitr", "scales", "vegan")
bioc_pkg <- c("ANCOMBC", "ape", "DESeq2",  "DirichletMultinomial", "mia", "miaViz")

# Gets those packages that are already installed
cran_pkg_already_installed <- cran_pkg[ cran_pkg %in% installed.packages() ]
bioc_pkg_already_installed <- bioc_pkg[ bioc_pkg %in% installed.packages() ]

# Gets those packages that need to be installed
cran_pkg_to_be_installed <- setdiff(cran_pkg, cran_pkg_already_installed)
bioc_pkg_to_be_installed <- setdiff(bioc_pkg, bioc_pkg_already_installed)
```

```{r}
# If there are packages that need to be installed, installs them from CRAN
if( length(cran_pkg_to_be_installed) ) {
  install.packages(cran_pkg_to_be_installed)
}
```

```{r}
# If there are packages that need to be installed, installs them from Bioconductor
if( length(bioc_pkg_to_be_installed) ) {
  BiocManager::install(bioc_pkg_to_be_installed, ask = F)
}
```

Now all required packages are installed, so let’s load them into the session. Some function names occur in multiple packages. That is why miaverse’s packages mia and miaViz are prioritized. Packages that are loaded first have higher priority.

```{r}
# Reorders bioc packages, so that mia and miaViz are first
bioc_pkg <- c(bioc_pkg[ bioc_pkg %in% c("mia", "miaViz") ], 
              bioc_pkg[ !bioc_pkg %in% c("mia", "miaViz") ] ) 

# Loading all packages into session. Returns true if package was successfully loaded.
loaded <- sapply(c(bioc_pkg, cran_pkg), require, character.only = TRUE)
as.data.frame(loaded)
```

## Data Importation

Data Access;

Option 1; Gut Microbiota from persons with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder affects the brain in mice

Loading Data into R....

```{r}
library(mia)
library(miaViz)
library(dplyr)
se <- readRDS("data/se.rds")
tse <- readRDS("data/tse.rds")
```

Microbiome Data Exploration,

Basic operations for data exploration to confirm that the data has all the necessary components:

```{r}
#Need to investigate how taxonomic profiling data is organized in R

dim(tse)
#Dimensionality tells us how many taxa and samples the data contains
```

There are 151 taxa and 27 samples.

```{r}
#rowData slot contains a taxonomic table. This includes the taxonomic information for the 151 entries. 
#The head command prints just the beginning of the table.
knitr::kable(head(rowData(tse))) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped", 
                            latex_options="scale_down") %>% 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

rowData contains information from 6 different taxonomy classes.

```{r}
#coLData slot contains sample metadata

#It has information for all 27 samples. 

#With the head commanded, the first 6 samples will be shown. 

#shows us the columns that contain information. 

knitr::kable(head(colData(tse))) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped", 
                            latex_options="scale_down") %>% 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

We can draw summaries from the sample (column) data.

Patient Status Distribution:

```{r}
#colData(tse)$patient_status fetches the data from the column.
#table() creates a table that shows how many times each class is present
#sort() sorts the tables to ascending order.
sort(table(colData(tse)$patient_status))
```

There are 13 patients with ADHD and 14 control samples.

**Data Transformations:**

Microbial abundances are typically ‘compositional’ (relative) in the current microbiome profiling data sets. This is due to technical aspects of the data generation process.

Calculating relative abundances:

```{r}
#relative abundance is easier to interpret than plain counts. 
#We need to transform the data into other formats.
# Calculates relative abundances, and stores the table to assays
tse <- transformAssay(tse, method = "relabundance")
```

Aggregation:

Microbial species can be called at multiple taxonomic resolutions. We can easily agglomerate the data based on taxonomic ranks. Here, we agglomerate the data at Phylum level.

```{r}
tse_phylum <- agglomerateByRank(tse, rank = "Phylum")

# Show dimensionality
dim(tse_phylum)
```

There are 5 taxa and 27 samples. undefinedundefined
